title: Course Description – Western States 100
claims: The Run starts at Olympic Valley, California, and ends in Auburn, California.
The Run begins at 5:00 a.m. on the Saturday of the last full weekend in June at the west end of Olympic Valley.
Runners must reach the finish line no later than 10:59:59 a.m. on the following day to be eligible for an award.
The valley floor at the start is 6,200 ft and Emigrant Pass is 8,750 ft, a climb of 2,550 vertical feet in the first 4.5 miles.
After Emigrant Pass the course climbs another 15,540 ft and descends 22,970 ft before reaching Auburn.
The Run follows the same basic course used since 1986 unless snow conditions force a route change.
The race uses the middle portion of the Western States Trail, a trail that stretches from Salt Lake City, Utah, to Sacramento, California.
Temperatures during the Run can range from 20 degrees to above 110 degrees Fahrenheit.
At 78 miles runners must ford the American River near the Rucky Chucky crossing; a guide rope is stretched across the river and rafts are used in high-water years.
There are dry stretches of over 8 miles during the Run and of 16 or more miles during training runs.
Almost half of the trail may be travelled at night and each runner should carry two LED flashlights.
Runners who drop before the Foresthill aid station are taken to Foresthill; runners who drop after Foresthill are taken to the finish line, and non-emergency evacuation may take several hours.
Aid stations close when the sweeps arrive.
Trail markings consist of pink surveyor's tape, W.S. Trail signs, arrows, signs and reflectors along the last 38 miles.
Much of the territory is accessible only by foot, horse or helicopter.
Approximately 1,500 volunteers help at each Western States Endurance Run.
